`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

`cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go:646` (the `created.Empty` short-circuit) and `:672` (`awaitMirrorReady`).

`awaitMirrorPlacement` (`cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_probe.go:112-121`) synthesizes `CreatedMirror` from `MirrorRequestResult`, which only carries `mirrorId/mirrorUrl/publicUrl` (`internal/coreapi/oas_schemas_gen.go:6367`). So `created.Empty` and `created.Suspended` are always `false` in async mode, and both short-circuits at `repo_mirror.go:642` / `:646` become dead.

Cost: for an empty upstream — the case the sync path explicitly documents as "nothing to clone, so don't poll for 'ready' — it never would" — the async path falls into `awaitMirrorReady` and polls `GetMirror` every 2s for the default 30-minute `--wait-timeout`: ~900 wasted control-plane calls per mirror, multiplied by `mirrorCreateConcurrency` in the wizard, ending in a spurious timeout error instead of the immediate "nothing to clone" exit. (Suspended is cheaper: one extra poll, since `awaitMirrorReady` returns `errMirrorSuspended` on the first read.)

Cheaper: carry `empty`/`suspended`/`created` through `MirrorRequestResult` and populate them in `awaitMirrorPlacement`, or — if the API can't carry them yet — do the one best-effort `GetMirror` before entering the clone poll and treat a non-`processing`/non-`ready` status as terminal.

### 2. First placement poll always waits a full 2s tick
`cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_probe.go:104` + `:132-139` — the loop checks the initial 202 body, then unconditionally blocks on `<-ticker.C` before the first `GetMirrorRequest`.

Cost: the async route replaces one blocking `CreateMirror` with submit + poll, and adds a hard 2s floor to placement even when the server finished the request in ~200ms. That is a directly user-visible 0–2s regression on every `repo mirror create` with the toggle on (and on the wizard's first line update). Note `awaitMirrorReady` (`:234-240`) does *not* have this problem — it polls immediately, then ticks.

Cheaper: poll at a short initial interval (e.g. 250ms) backing off to `mirrorPollInterval`, or at minimum do one immediate `GetMirrorRequest` before entering the ticker loop.

### 3. Phase de-duplication implemented twice
`cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go:524-534` (`onPhase` compares `next == phase`) and `:578-585` (`reportPhase` compares `phase == currentPhase`) both suppress repeated phases; the wizard's callback at `repo_mirror_create_wizard.go:575` relies only on the inner one.

Cost: zero runtime cost (three phase transitions total) — flagging only because the outer guard is redundant state the one-shot caller has to keep in sync. Drop the `next == phase` check in `newRepoMirrorCreateCmd` and let `createAndAwaitMirror` own the dedup.

### 4. Minor: settings load runs before argument validation
`cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go:493-496` — `LoadEntireSettings` runs first thing in `RunE`, ahead of `parseGitHubURL` and `validateClusterHost`.

Cost: `settings.Load` forks `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and reads up to three JSON layers (`settings.go:555-573`, uncached), so a typo'd URL pays a subprocess before failing. Single-digit milliseconds against a command that then does cluster discovery plus HTTP, so this is only worth moving if you're touching the block anyway — load it after validation, or lazily in the two branches that use it.


Every `*coreapi.Client` is built with `newCrossJurisHTTPClient()` (`internal/coreapi/client.go:148`), and `canonicalizeMirrorRequestLocation` (`cross_juris_transport.go:308`) rewrites Scheme+Host on *every* 202 from `/api/v1/mirror-requests`. It threads `ctx` through five return statements just to hand it back unchanged on every error path, and mixes URL parsing with `coreapi.WithServerURL` injection. Cost: a 3-value signature where 2 would do, and `ctx` shadowing at the call site (`:96`). Simpler: `func mirrorRequestPollTarget(location string) (serverURL *url.URL, requestID uuid.UUID, err error)`, with `awaitMirrorPlacement` doing `ctx = coreapi.WithServerURL(ctx, serverURL)`. Also, the four identical `fmt.Errorf("invalid mirror request Location %q", location)` returns can collapse to a single labelled/`invalid:` exit.

`classifyWaitContextErr` (`repo_mirror_probe.go:286`), `classifyPlacementWaitContextErr` (`repo_mirror_probe.go:276`), and the inline block in `createAndAwaitMirror` (`repo_mirror.go:607-615`) are byte-for-byte the same shape — `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) → NewSilentError`, else `fmt.Errorf("timed out <phrase>: %w")` — differing only in the phrase. Simpler: `classifyWaitContextErr(err error, what string) error` and three call sites passing `"submitting mirror request"` / `"waiting for mirror placement"` / `"waiting for initial clone"`.

Simpler: make the async case print `"\nMirror placed\n"` and let the shared `fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", created.MirrorUrl)` run unconditionally (or give each case its own full block and delete the second `if`). Separately, the field itself is exactly `opts.async`, which both call sites already know — it exists only so `reportOneShotMirror` needn't take another param, which is defensible, but worth naming as duplicated state.

Async wraps the whole operation in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, opts.timeout)` and then must *neutralize* the same timeout at the clone poll (`pollTimeout = 0`); sync leaves the context alone and passes `opts.timeout` into `awaitMirrorReady`. A reader has to hold both paths in their head to answer "what is bounded by `--wait-timeout`?". Simpler (if the behavior change is acceptable): always derive `waitCtx` from `opts.timeout` and always call `awaitMirrorReady(waitCtx, ..., 0)`. That does make the sync `CreateMirror` call deadline-bounded too, which it currently is not — flag it as a deliberate choice rather than an accident if you keep the split.

**8. `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_create_wizard.go:509, 563 — `asyncMirrorRequests` is threaded as a 7th/8th positional bool.**
`createOneMirror(ctx, t, c, clientErr, noWait, waitTimeout, asyncMirrorRequests, report)` has two adjacent bare `bool`s at the call site (`:542`, and `false` in three tests), and the three values are forwarded verbatim into `mirrorCreateOptions` at `:573`. Cost: positional-bool call sites that read as `..., nil, false, time.Second, false, nil`. Cost: this is only safe today because of finding 2 — the transport rewrites `Location`'s host to the host that actually served the request, so the CLI can never be pointed off-federation. Deeper fix: origin pinning belongs in `internal/coreapi` (a client method or a documented `coreapi` helper that takes the raw `Location` and applies the same federation/scheme gate as `followMisdirected`), not in a `cmd/` probe file.

**2. `internal/coreapi/cross_juris_transport.go:305-317` — `canonicalizeMirrorRequestLocation` is a per-endpoint patch inside shared transport code.**

## Applied (net −114 lines, all within the branch's files)

**Production code**
- **Unified the three copies of the canceled-vs-timeout classifier** into one `classifyWaitContextErr(err, what)` (`repo_mirror_probe.go:276`). The placement poll, the clone poll, and the inline block in the async submit path all called the same shape with different wording; `classifyPlacementWaitContextErr` is gone and the error messages are unchanged.
- **Removed the duplicate phase de-duplication** in the one-shot command's spinner callback (`repo_mirror.go:526`) — `createAndAwaitMirror`'s `reportPhase` already guarantees distinct phases — and the redundant `lastStatus` guard inside `awaitMirrorPlacement`, leaving one de-dup point.
- **`mirrorCreatePhase.label()` now calls the existing `upperFirst` helper** instead of re-implementing capitalization with byte slicing (which would panic on an empty phase and mishandle multi-byte runes).
- **`mirrorRequestPollTarget` is now a pure parser** returning `(serverURL, requestID, error)` instead of threading a `context.Context` through five returns; the caller applies `coreapi.WithServerURL`. Also dropped the provably dead `!strings.HasPrefix(path, "/")` clause (the path already survived `CutPrefix("/api/v1/...")`); the scheme-relative-URL rejection (`Host != ""` without a scheme) stays.
- **Replaced the `noWait, waitTimeout, asyncMirrorRequests` positional-parameter chain** through `runMirrorCreateWizard` → `createMirrors` → `createOneMirror` with the `mirrorCreateOptions` struct the branch already introduced; `RunE` builds it once and `createOneMirror` sets its per-target `onPhase`.

**Tests (`repo_mirror_request_test.go`, −150 lines)**
- Deleted `wireJSON` — the hand-maintained wire-format maps duplicated the generated ogen marshalers and would silently drift from the spec; handlers now serve `&coreapi.MirrorRequest{...}` / `&coreapi.Mirror{...}` through `printJSON`, the same pattern `serveMirrorCreate` already uses. The pass-through `writeMirrorRequest` and `writeMirrorRequestBody` went with it.
- Added `newMirrorRequestClient(t, handler)` and replaced the 13 copies of the four-line server/client bootstrap.
- Three tests that inlined `useFastMirrorPolling`'s exact body now call it.
- `TestRepoMirrorCreate_AsyncSetting` now uses the existing `setupTestRepo`/`writeSettings` helpers — this also fixes a latent test-ordering hazard: the hand-rolled scaffolding did `t.Chdir` without clearing the worktree-root cache.

## Skipped, with reasons

- **Async path can poll an empty upstream for the full 30-min timeout** (the synthesized `CreatedMirror` never carries `Empty`/`Suspended`, so those short-circuits are dead in async mode, and the wizard's `mirrorStatusEmpty` path is unreachable). Real gap, but the fix needs the API to carry those facts in `MirrorRequestResult` (or an extra `GetMirror` probe) — a behavior/design change, not a cleanup. Worth a follow-up issue.
- **Unknown-failure-code allow-list** in `mirrorRequestFailureError`: the review-feedback commit ("preserve diagnostics for unknown placement failures") deliberately kept this distinction, so I left it.
- **Inline `LoadEntireSettings` error-swallow** instead of a `settings.IsAsyncMirrorRequestsEnabled` accessor: also shaped by that review round ("keeping exempt mirror creation available when repository settings cannot be loaded"), and pinned by `TestRepoMirrorCreate_BrokenEntireDirUsesDefaultRoute`.
- **`--wait-timeout` meaning whole-operation in async but clone-only in sync**, and the `Location` canonicalization living as a per-endpoint branch in the shared cross-juris transport (vs. server-side 421 support or a generic effective-origin mechanism): both are deliberate design choices on this branch; changing them alters behavior/trust boundaries. The altitude agent's deeper-fix suggestions are good candidates for the PR description or follow-ups, not a simplify pass.
- **First placement poll waits one full 2s tick**: the 202 body already carries the initial status, so the "waste" is at most 2s ahead of a clone that takes minutes — not worth restructuring the loop.
- Minor items left alone: the settings-test table (touched by the review round), the `writeCoreProblem`/`writeNotFoundProblem` pair (dedup would touch a file outside the branch), and the `/api/v1/mirror-requests` path literal appearing in both packages (exporting a constant adds surface for little drift protection).
